subject: Customer inquiry: VPC custody, customer-led purge & escrow options

Subject: Questions on VPC custody, customer-led purge & escrow options

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — Cardinal Health’s infrastructure team asked for a short write-up on how Redwood handles private/VPC deployments where the customer controls storage and demands:

- Verifiable proof-of-delete (what evidence do you provide?)
- Option for an encrypted escrow snapshot we can retrieve if needed
- KMS/HSM integration and key-wrap/zeroization guarantees
- Timing guarantees for tombstoning and irreversible deletion after a customer-initiated purge

We're preparing our security checklist for our regulated business units and need concise answers so we can feed them to Procurement and Legal. Also: any sample attestation artifacts you can share would be helpful.

Thanks,
Sam Teller
Sr. Cloud Ops Engineer
Cardinal Health

(P.S. happy to hop on a quick call if that speeds things up)
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Questions on VPC custody, customer-led purge & escrow options

Sam — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; I’ve looped in Marissa (security & product) for technical attestation detail and Dev for ops cadence.

1) Proof-of-delete: we provide deletion runbooks, system event logs (immutable, tamper-evident write-once entries), and a signed cryptographic digest (SHA-256) of the deleted snapshot(s) that our KMS signs with an AWS KMS / HSM-backed key. The signed digest plus the log entries serve as an auditable artifact.

2) Encrypted escrow snapshots: we offer an optional encrypted snapshot escrow where a customer-approved public key wraps the snapshot. Escrow retention is configurable (default 90 days) and the snapshot is stored encrypted at rest; only the customer holds the private key to unwrap. Access requests require the documented retrieval flow & approval.

3) KMS/HSM: Redwood supports customer-managed keys (CMKs) in supported clouds plus on-prem HSM integrations for private deployments. Key zeroization: upon key deletion we follow the platform zeroization process and provide attestations of the key lifecycle event.

4) Timing and tombstoning: For private/VPC deployments we respect customer retention policies. When a purge is initiated we tombstone the tenant marker immediately (within seconds) and begin background garbage collection. Irreversible deletion of persistent replicas and snapshots completes within the SLA window (default 30 days) unless you request accelerated deletion (we can schedule an expedited wipe during a maintenance window).

I’ve attached a short Q&A playbook and will ask Marissa to add the sample attestation artifacts. What regulatory requirements (HIPAA / 21 CFR / other) should we account for? If you want, propose a 30-minute slot and we’ll run through the artifacts.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference

Sam — adding technical specifics and concrete artifacts. Attaching the playbook (redwood_vpc_erase_playbook_v2.pdf) and a small example attestation (crypto-attestation-sample.txt). Highlights below.

Proof-of-delete (detail):
- We create a snapshot manifest for every persistent snapshot that includes snapshot id, CIDR of storage node, timestamp, and content hash (SHA-256 per-file + aggregated manifest hash).
- Upon deletion we append a deletion record to an append-only ledger (immutable service) which includes the manifest hash and deletion event metadata (who/when/trigger).
- The manifest hash is signed by a KMS-backed key; the signed token is provided as the attestation artifact.

Escrow snapshot flow (detail):
- At customer request we generate an encrypted export. The export is encrypted client-side with customer-provided public key (RSA-4096 / EC-384) and escrowed to an isolated object bucket in the customer VPC or a mutually agreed storage endpoint.
- Retrieval requires an authenticated retrieval request from a whitelisted cardinal operator identity plus a customer governance approval (e.g., signed DocuSign request). We log the retrieval event and produce a signed retrieval audit.

KMS/HSM & key management:
- Support for BYOK via cloud KMS, and HSM integration for on-prem private deployments. Keys used for signing attestations are rotated on a configurable schedule; rotations are recorded and available for audit.
- When a key is destroyed we generate a key-destruction attestation including the key id, destruction timestamp, and HSM transaction id.

Deletion timing & irreversible wipe:
- Tombstone: immediate marker set in config (seconds).
- Background GC: node-level deletion begins within 24 hours; full deletion across replicated stores completes within the SLA window (default 30 days).
- Accelerated wipe: available — we run a multi-pass overwrite (where supported) and mark dependent caches and backups for purge. We provide a deletion completion report and the signed artifact.

Compliance notes: we can produce artifacts suitable for HIPAA and SOC2 evidence packages; for 21 CFR we recommend a runbook that includes your procedural approvals (we can mirror your control IDs).

Attachments: redwood_vpc_erase_playbook_v2.pdf (playbook), crypto-attestation-sample.txt (signed digest example).

If you want a hands-on demo of an escrow retrieval + attestation, we can run a canary with a non-prod tenant in your presence.

— Marissa Cole
Product Security Lead | Redwood Inference
